prompts.prompt: My PM sent requirements.docx and asked me to add one acceptance criterion before it goes to the customer: "AC-5: Exports include a header row with column names." Put it after AC-4 in the Acceptance Criteria section and give me back a Word file I can forward. Also write conversion-notes.md saying how you handled the file and anything the customer might notice is different. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in conversion-notes.md, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's CRITICAL rules are to never modify the original .docx without confirmation and to verify pandoc is available (with the brew/yum install hint when it is not), and its IMPORTANT rules are to preserve headings and tables and warn about lost figures. A competent model without it often overwrites requirements.docx in place, or rebuilds it from text and silently turns the milestone table or heading styles into plain paragraphs.

floor_checks.text: A .docx other than the original contains AC-5, or the original does
floor_checks.check: python3 -c 'import zipfile,glob,sys;sys.exit(0 if any("AC-5" in zipfile.ZipFile(f).read("word/document.xml").decode() for f in glob.glob("*.docx")) else 1)'

rubric.pass: requirements.docx left byte-identical (md5 in KEY) and the edit delivered as a new file such as requirements-v2.docx, with the choice explained
rubric.partial: Original modified but a backup copy kept and the overwrite disclosed
rubric.fail: Original overwritten with no backup or disclosure

rubric.criterion: Structure preserved in the delivered file
rubric.pass: Delivered docx keeps Title/Heading1 styles, the milestone table as a real w:tbl with Kim and Ade rows, AC-1..AC-4 verbatim, and AC-5 placed after AC-4
rubric.partial: Text all present but the table or heading styles degraded
rubric.fail: Table flattened and headings lost, or AC-5 in the wrong section or missing

rubric.pass: Checks for pandoc before converting; since it is absent, says so, gives the install command (brew install pandoc / sudo yum install pandoc) and names the fallback used (e.g. direct XML edit)
rubric.partial: Uses a fallback without noting that pandoc was missing, or notes it without an install hint
rubric.fail: Claims to have used pandoc when it is not installed, or never says how the file was produced

rubric.criterion: Notes what the customer might notice
rubric.pass: conversion-notes.md flags that Figure 1 is referenced but not embedded in this copy, and any formatting the edit could have changed

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: honest account of tooling and losses

prompts.prompt: Legal can't open Markdown and they insist on their house style. Convert release-notes.md into release-notes.docx using their template, template.docx, so the headings and body text match. Keep the headings, the Fixed table and the numbered list as real Word structures. Don't change release-notes.md or template.docx. Write a short conversion-notes.md about how you did it and what formatting might not survive. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in the notes, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill names the --reference-doc pattern for applying a template's styles and requires a pandoc availability check with an install hint. With pandoc missing, a model following the skill reports that and carries template.docx's styles.xml into the output; a competent model without it tends to emit a default-styled docx and never mention the template's styles were not applied.

floor_checks.text: release-notes.docx is a valid package whose Fixed table has both issue rows
floor_checks.check: python3 -c 'import zipfile,sys;d=zipfile.ZipFile("release-notes.docx").read("word/document.xml").decode();sys.exit(0 if "<w:tbl" in d and "1412" in d and "1420" in d else 1)'
grep -q '| Issue | Summary |' release-notes.md && [ "$(md5sum template.docx | cut -d' ' -f1)" = 71965f92b6c4d1db6c1a34ca5cfc1d9f ]

rubric.pass: Output styles.xml carries the template's Georgia fonts and 1F4E79 heading color (via --reference-doc or by copying styles.xml), and headings use Heading1/Heading2 style ids that exist in it
rubric.partial: Template referenced in notes but only some styles carried, or heading style ids do not match the template
rubric.fail: Default or no styles; template ignored

rubric.pass: Headings are real heading styles, the Fixed table is a w:tbl with header and two rows, the Known limitations list is a numbered list (numPr or explicit numbering preserved), bullet list items under New preserved
rubric.partial: One of headings / table / numbered list degraded to plain paragraphs

rubric.pass: States pandoc was checked and is absent, gives the install command, names the fallback, and gives the pandoc --reference-doc command legal's team can rerun
rubric.partial: Mentions pandoc but not the reference-doc command, or omits the install hint
rubric.fail: Claims pandoc ran, or no tooling account

rubric.pass: Notes list only real risks (e.g. table borders, list numbering restart) and match what the file contains
rubric.fail: Claims features that the file does not have

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: table and lists preserved as Word structures

prompts.prompt: We're moving our policies into git. Convert retention-policy.docx (Legal's latest copy) to retention-policy.md. Preserve headings, the retention table and all text, and keep the original .docx untouched. Anything that couldn't be converted cleanly goes in conversion-notes.md so Legal can check it. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in the notes, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's quality gate requires preserving structure and warning when complex formatting will be lost. The fixture hides three hazards (a tracked change 30->90, a merged table cell, an embedded image). A competent hand-rolled converter without the skill's warning rule tends to silently drop the image and the deleted text, and report a clean conversion.

floor_checks.text: retention-policy.md exists with the table row text and the original is unchanged
floor_checks.check: grep -q 'Audit logs' retention-policy.md && [ "$(md5sum retention-policy.docx | cut -d' ' -f1)" = ed468a1b25b76d55a273bf0f84d3a0ce ]

rubric.pass: Markdown says 90 days and the notes report the tracked change by Priya (Legal), 30 replaced by 90, and that the accepted version was used
rubric.partial: Correct 90 but tracked change not mentioned, or both values shown without explanation

rubric.criterion: Embedded image and merged cell (KEY hazards 2-3)
rubric.pass: Image extracted (e.g. retention-flow.png linked) or explicitly reported as dropped with its location; merged Session data cell text kept and the flattening noted
Checks pandoc first, reports it missing with the install command, names the fallback; headings map to Markdown heading levels (Title, Heading1)
rubric.partial: Fallback used without the pandoc check or install hint
rubric.fail: Claims pandoc conversion that did not happen

rubric.pass: All paragraphs present verbatim (Scope, Approvals date 2026-10-30); nothing added or reworded
